value.rationale: The minimum enclosing-circle radius of a random planar shadow is a canonical geometric projection functional, distinct from width and brightness. Its exact nontrivial high-tail law exposes four tetrahedral axes, six correlated great-circle belt intersections and a sharp three-way overlap threshold at radius \(\sqrt{8/3}\), as well as a distinctive square-root endpoint exponent with an explicit intersection correction. The particular invariant is motivated by radial enclosure under random views; the claim is stronger than a small routine moment calculation and does not merely adjust a previously known parameter.
